name: Can any interior wall be removed to create an open floor plan?

mainEntity.name: Can any interior wall be removed to create an open floor plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tearing down a wall depends entirely on whether it is load-bearing or a simple partition wall. Non-bearing partition walls can usually be removed with standard interior demolition and basic reframing around surrounding surfaces. Load-bearing walls support the weight of the roof or floors above, requiring temporary support walls, an engineered beam, and dedicated structural posts before removal. During an on-site assessment, we evaluate the floor joist orientation, attic structure, and basement supports below to determine if a wall is structural, ensuring your home remains stable before any studs are cut.
acceptedAnswer.description: Non-bearing walls can be removed easily, but load-bearing walls require temporary shoring and structural support beams to safely hold upper floor loads.
